Lab 13: Managing Ceph Authentication with CephX
Objectives
By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

Understand the CephX authentication mechanism and its security benefits
Configure CephX authentication for secure client and service communication
Create and manage Ceph client credentials and keyrings
Implement proper access control policies for different user types
Test authentication mechanisms and troubleshoot common issues
Validate data security through controlled access testing
Prerequisites
Before starting this lab, students should have:

Basic understanding of Ceph storage architecture
Familiarity with Linux command-line operations
Knowledge of file permissions and user management concepts
Understanding of public-key cryptography basics
Completed previous Ceph labs or equivalent experience
Access to a functioning Ceph cluster (minimum 3 nodes)
Lab Environment
Ready-to-Use Cloud Machines: Al Nafi provides pre-configured Linux-based cloud machines with Ceph already installed. Simply click Start Lab to begin - no need to build your own virtual machines or install software.

Your lab environment includes:

3 Ceph nodes (ceph-node1, ceph-node2, ceph-node3)
Pre-installed Ceph Octopus or newer version
Administrative access to all nodes
Network connectivity between all nodes
Task 1: Set up CephX for Secure Client and Service Authentication
Subtask 1.1: Verify Current Authentication Status
First, let's examine the current authentication configuration in your Ceph cluster.

Connect to the admin node:
ssh ceph-admin@ceph-node1
Check current authentication settings:
ceph auth list
Verify cluster authentication configuration:
ceph config get mon auth_cluster_required
ceph config get mon auth_service_required
ceph config get mon auth_client_required
Display current cluster status:
ceph -s
Subtask 1.2: Enable CephX Authentication
If CephX is not already enabled, we'll configure it properly.

Set authentication requirements for all components:
ceph config set global auth_cluster_required cephx
ceph config set global auth_service_required cephx
ceph config set global auth_client_required cephx
Verify the authentication settings:
ceph config dump | grep auth
Restart Ceph services to apply changes (if needed):
sudo systemctl restart ceph-mon@$(hostname)
sudo systemctl restart ceph-mgr@$(hostname)
sudo systemctl restart ceph-osd@*
Subtask 1.3: Understand CephX Key Management
Examine the admin keyring:
sudo cat /etc/ceph/ceph.client.admin.keyring
List all authentication keys:
ceph auth list
Check monitor keyring:
sudo ceph-authtool --list /etc/ceph/ceph.mon.keyring
Task 2: Manage Ceph Client Credentials
Subtask 2.1: Create Custom Client Users
Now we'll create different types of client users with specific permissions.

Create a read-only client user:
ceph auth get-or-create client.readonly mon 'allow r' osd 'allow r'
Create a client user with pool-specific access:
# First, create a test pool if it doesn't exist
ceph osd pool create testpool 32 32

# Create user with access only to testpool
ceph auth get-or-create client.testuser mon 'allow r' osd 'allow rw pool=testpool'
Create a backup client with broader permissions:
ceph auth get-or-create client.backup mon 'allow r' osd 'allow rw' mds 'allow rw'
Verify the new users were created:
ceph auth list | grep client
Subtask 2.2: Export and Manage Keyrings
Export individual client keyrings:
# Export readonly client keyring
ceph auth get client.readonly -o /tmp/ceph.client.readonly.keyring

# Export testuser client keyring
ceph auth get client.testuser -o /tmp/ceph.client.testuser.keyring

# Export backup client keyring
ceph auth get client.backup -o /tmp/ceph.client.backup.keyring
Verify keyring contents:
cat /tmp/ceph.client.readonly.keyring
cat /tmp/ceph.client.testuser.keyring
cat /tmp/ceph.client.backup.keyring
Create a combined keyring file:
# Create a new keyring with multiple clients
sudo ceph-authtool --create-keyring /tmp/ceph.client.combined.keyring

# Add clients to the combined keyring
sudo ceph-authtool /tmp/ceph.client.combined.keyring --import-keyring /tmp/ceph.client.readonly.keyring
sudo ceph-authtool /tmp/ceph.client.combined.keyring --import-keyring /tmp/ceph.client.testuser.keyring

# Verify combined keyring
sudo ceph-authtool --list /tmp/ceph.client.combined.keyring
Subtask 2.3: Modify Client Permissions
Update permissions for an existing client:
# Add MDS permissions to testuser
ceph auth caps client.testuser mon 'allow r' osd 'allow rw pool=testpool' mds 'allow r'
Verify the permission changes:
ceph auth get client.testuser
Create a client with time-limited access (using caps):
# Create a temporary user with limited scope
ceph auth get-or-create client.temporary mon 'allow r' osd 'allow rw pool=testpool'
Task 3: Test Access Control and Data Security
Subtask 3.1: Test Read-Only Access
Test the readonly client:
# Try to list pools with readonly client
ceph --id readonly osd lspools

# Try to create a pool (this should fail)
ceph --id readonly osd pool create unauthorized-pool 32 32
Test object operations with readonly client:
# Create a test object using admin credentials
echo "test data" | rados -p testpool put test-object -

# Try to read the object with readonly client
rados --id readonly -p testpool get test-object /tmp/readonly-test.txt
cat /tmp/readonly-test.txt

# Try to write with readonly client (this should fail)
echo "unauthorized write" | rados --id readonly -p testpool put unauthorized-object -
Subtask 3.2: Test Pool-Specific Access
Test testuser access to authorized pool:
# This should work - testuser has access to testpool
echo "authorized data" | rados --id testuser -p testpool put authorized-object -

# Verify the object was created
rados --id testuser -p testpool ls
Test testuser access to unauthorized pool:
# Create another pool for testing
ceph osd pool create restrictedpool 32 32

# Try to access restrictedpool with testuser (this should fail)
echo "unauthorized data" | rados --id testuser -p restrictedpool put unauthorized-object -
Verify access restrictions:
# List what pools testuser can see
rados --id testuser lspools

echo "[client.fake]" > /tmp/fake.keyring
